title: Gradual model admittance capacity budget
body:
Purpose:
This is a capacity-budget worksheet for a gradual, traffic-gated onboarding of a new medium-large open model variant (codenamed: halcyon-13B) across three regions. Goal is to define an admission curve, per-region KV cache slice allocations, and hard action triggers so we can avoid eviction storms and maintain 99th pct latency SLOs during the first 30 days after soft-launch.

Quick take (one paragraph):
We expect the model to increase per-request KV footprint by ~3.2x compared to baseline 7B family traffic due to longer context and larger key-value rows. With conservative admission (0->25% of existing 7B ingress requests over 14 days) and region-weighted capacity routing, the fleet should absorb the load with a 15% headroom requirement. If regional KV occupancy exceeds 78% for more than 2 hours, trigger admission rollback and a forced redistribution of cache slices.

Assumptions (sources and numbers):
- Model: halcyon-13B (int8 quant).
- Typical requests: mean seq_len=1024 tokens, median kv-rows/request=1.9 MB, peak 4.8 MB.
- Baseline 7B KV density per GPU: 38 GB resident. New model effective KV delta per active session: +2.4 GB.
- GPU slot equivalence: 1 slot = 40 RPS sustained at seq_len=1024.
- Regional replication factors and current reserved safety: us-west-2 has 48 slots free, us-east-1 has 36, eu-west-1 has 22.
- Eviction tolerance target: keep tail eviction events < 0.1% of active requests.

Regional capacity snapshot (derived from monitoring sample 2026-02-07 to 2026-02-09):
Region | GPU nodes | Effective slots | Current util | Reserved (other models) | KV capacity (GB) | Avail for halcyon (GB)
us-west-2 | 120 | 240 | 72% | 40 slots | 4,800 GB | 1,150 GB
us-east-1 | 90 | 180 | 80% | 36 slots | 3,600 GB | 680 GB
eu-west-1 | 56 | 112 | 68% | 16 slots | 2,240 GB | 420 GB

Interpretation: us-west-2 has the most headroom in slots and KV; eu-west-1 is the tightest. We intentionally over-assign admission weight to us-west-2 during ramp to reduce eviction risk.

Admittance curve (recommended, conservative):
Day 0-2: 0.5% of equivalent 7B requests (smoke + sanity checks) -> target active sessions: 40 global
Day 3-6: 2% -> 160 active
Day 7-10: 6% -> 480 active
Day 11-14: 12% -> 960 active
Day 15-21: 18% -> 1,440 active
Day 22-30: 25% -> 2,000 active (plateau, reassess)
Routing weight: us-west-2: 55%, us-east-1: 30%, eu-west-1: 15% during ramp. Rebalance to 45/35/20 if us-east-1 observed latency spike < 99th pct threshold.

Expected KV growth by day (global aggregated):
Day 0: +0.0 GB
Day 6: +380 GB
Day 14: +1,200 GB
Day 21: +2,000 GB
Day 30: +2,800 GB
Note: these numbers include active-session share only; background warmups (seeded warmup traffic) are budgeted separately (+~220 GB by day 10).

Eviction sensitivity table (probabilistic):
KV occupancy | Predicted eviction spike probability | Immediate mitigation
< 62% | ~0.01% | none
62-70% | ~0.05% | reduce admission slope by 20% (next 24h)
70-78% | ~0.3% | pause new session admits for region, redirect new traffic to other regions
>78% | >1% | immediate rollback to previous stable traffic % and clear warmup queues, notify SRE

Safety margins and triggers (automated):
- Automated circuit: if any region's KV occupancy > 75% for 60 continuous minutes -> auto-slow admit (cut scheduled admits by 50%).
- If occupancy > 78% for 120 minutes -> auto-rollback admit by 40% and escalate to on-call SRE + infra-eng slack channel (#infra-oncall).
- If 99th latency increases by >20% vs baseline for >30m -> route 30% of traffic to fallback model and pause further admits.

Operational play (checklist):
- Pre-launch (S-3 days): seed 2% of final warmup set in us-west-2 (ticket INFRA-1723). Verify kv-allocator dry-run.
- Launch Day: enable Day 0-2 admits, monitor KV occupancy, 95/99 latency, and eviction metrics. Stand up a 1-hrly cadence for first 12 hours.
- Day 3-14: follow admission curve, weekly triage with product/solutions to validate quality regressions.
- Day 15-30: if stable, increase regional weight to improve latency in eu-west-1; if unstable, apply rollback and run a focused memory profiling PR (linked).

Quick capacity delta actions (what to do if we hit triggers):
- Short term (minutes): reduce admission percentages via feature flag (admit-percentage var), move admission weight to us-west-2, purge non-essential KV preloads.
- Medium term (hours): bump reserved slots in region (if commit available), spin up temporary burst nodes in nearest zone, extend cache eviction TTLs conservatively.
- Long term (days): request procurement of +20 GPU nodes for eu-west-1 (procurement ticket), refine model KV quantization build to reduce per-session KV by target 18%.

Open questions & unknowns:
- Actual per-request KV rows distribution under real user prompts (current test set may underrepresent long-context sessions). Need sampling experiment (A/B sample id: sample-halcyon-0210).
- Efficiency trade-offs of more aggressive quantization (int4) vs degradation in generation quality for specific customer prompts. Product to surface prioritized eval prompts.

Metrics to plot in the launch dashboard (minimum):
- Regional KV occupancy (5m, 1h), global KV growth (cumulative GB), slot utilization by model family, 95/99 latency by region, eviction events per 10k requests, admit-% vs actual share, seeded-warmup progress.

Action owners & next steps:
- Aisha Patel (owner): finalize admit feature-flag knobs and coordinate SRE runbooks (due 2026-02-14).
- Marco Reyes: implement auto-slow circuit (PR #624), add telemetry hooks (due 2026-02-18).
- Sofia Liu: prepare warmup seed generator and sample set (due 2026-02-12).
- Ethan Kim: run sample profiling for KV delta across common prompts (due 2026-02-16).

Appendix: small reference calculations:
- New KV per active session = mean_kv_rows * average_row_size = 1.9 * 1.26 MB ~= 2.4 GB effect per active session after compression/quantization overheads.
- Effective available GB for halcyon in us-west-2 = KV capacity - (current resident for other models + reserved warmup margin) = 4800 - 3450 - 200 = 1150 GB.

Notes (informal):
- This is intentionally conservative; product wants faster ramp but we prioritized SLO stability.
- Keep this doc living in-drive while we iterate on numeric inputs from profiling runs.

References: linked tickets and profiling PRs above; slack thread #model-onboard-halcyon (search).
